answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the protocol deploys a dynamic staking barrier where every spawned identity must lock an atlas of verifiable state proofs alongside non-refundable cryptographic stake burning. The consensus channels flow like an incoming river into an economic jetty, strictly throttling registration bandwidth. Marginal minting burns scale at a superlinear cost factor of O(N^2.5), imposing catastrophic quadratic penalties that render mass identity replication economically unviable.
